generic_name: Emtricitabine, Rilpivirine, and Tenofovir Disoproxil Fumarate
drug_class: Combination Antiretroviral (HIV Medicine) — includes two NRTIs and one NNRTI
purpose: This medicine is used to treat HIV-1 infection in adults and certain adolescents. It helps lower the amount of HIV virus in your body so your immune system can stay stronger. It is not a cure for HIV, but it helps you stay healthier and reduces the risk of passing HIV to others.
how_it_works: This pill combines three different medicines that work together to block HIV from copying itself inside your body. Two of the medicines (emtricitabine and tenofovir) act like fake building blocks that HIV tries to use but cannot, stopping it from multiplying. The third medicine (rilpivirine) blocks a specific tool the virus needs to make copies of itself. Together, they keep the virus at very low levels in your blood.
common_side_effects: Some people may feel nauseous, have headaches, feel tired, or have trouble sleeping or unusual dreams, especially when first starting the medicine. Dizziness, depressed mood, and stomach upset can also happen. Most of these side effects tend to improve after the first few weeks.
warnings: Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, as stopping can allow the virus to multiply and become harder to treat. This medicine can sometimes cause serious liver or kidney problems, so your doctor will check your labs regularly. It should always be taken with a full meal — taking it without food may mean it does not work as well. Tell your doctor about all other medicines you take, as many drugs can interfere with this one. If you have hepatitis B, stopping this medicine can cause a serious flare-up of hepatitis.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one tablet taken by mouth once a day, always with a full meal (not just a snack). Try to take it at the same time every day to keep drug levels steady. Never skip doses or take extra doses to make up for a missed one — just take your next scheduled dose as normal.
